items.q: The Four Corners Monument is where Utah, Colorado, Arizona and which other state meet?
items.f: It's the only place in the U.S. where four states meet at one point.
items.s: NOAA National Geodetic Survey

items.q: At its northern end, California's Highway 1 meets US 101 near which small town?
items.f: The Pacific Coast Highway runs as Route 1 from southern Orange County all the way up the coast to Leggett.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: Pacific Coast Highway Byway

items.q: Utah's Scenic Byway 12 links Bryce Canyon with which other national park?
items.f: Watch for the Hogback, a narrow ridge with steep drop-offs on both sides of the road.
items.s: Visit Utah (Utah Office of Tourism)

items.q: Avenue of the Giants is a scenic drive through which trees?
items.f: The 32-mile drive through Humboldt Redwoods State Park follows the old route of Highway 101.
items.s: California State Parks

items.q: Which glacier can you see right from the Icefields Parkway?
items.f: It flows from the Columbia Icefield, the largest mass of glacial ice in the Canadian Rockies. Don't walk on it without a guide, because crevasses can be deadly.
items.s: Parks Canada: Travelling the Icefields Parkway

items.q: Road Trip Locals' 'Grand Trifecta' connects Grand Teton, Yellowstone and which other national park?
items.f: We recommend 10 to 14 days. Fly into Bozeman, head north from Grand Teton through Yellowstone, and finish in Glacier.
items.s: Road Trip Locals: The Grand Trifecta

items.q: What does your vehicle need to drive the Icefields Parkway from November 1 to March 31?
items.f: You also need a valid national parks pass to drive the parkway at any time of year.
items.s: Parks Canada: Icefields Parkway in Winter

items.q: In what year was Jack Kerouac's road trip novel 'On the Road' published?
items.f: Kerouac typed the first full draft in April 1951 on sheets taped into a scroll about 120 feet long.
items.s: New York Public Library

items.q: Work on the Blue Ridge Parkway began in 1935. When was it declared complete?
items.f: The dedication on September 11, 1987 ended a 14-mile detour around Grandfather Mountain.
items.s: National Park Service: History of the Linn Cove Viaduct

items.q: Glacier's Going-to-the-Sun Road crosses the Continental Divide at which pass?
items.f: There's no set opening date, because it depends on snow. The road is usually fully open by early July.
items.s: National Park Service: Going-to-the-Sun Road

items.q: The Natchez Trace Parkway runs from Natchez, Mississippi to near which city?
items.f: The parkway is 444 miles long, with mileposts running from 0 at Natchez to 444 near Nashville.
items.s: National Park Service: Natchez Trace Parkway

items.q: Trail Ridge Road links Estes Park with which Colorado town?
items.f: The 48-mile drive crosses Rocky Mountain National Park and tops out at 12,183 feet.
items.s: National Park Service: Trail Ridge Road

items.q: Route 66 originally ran between which two cities?
items.f: Route 66 got its number in 1926. Back then, almost none of it was paved.
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Overview

items.q: Which was the most visited site in the entire National Park System in 2025?
items.f: The Parkway recorded more than 16.5 million recreation visits, just ahead of Golden Gate.
items.s: National Park Service: 2025 Visitation Statistics

items.q: Why was the Alaska Highway built in 1942?
items.a: As a military route in World War II
items.f: Army engineers built the road from Dawson Creek, British Columbia, to Delta Junction, Alaska, in about eight months.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: Alaska Highway Fact Sheet

items.q: The Icefields Parkway links Lake Louise with which town?
items.f: The parkway (Highway 93 North) runs 232 km (144 miles), and there's only one gas station along the whole drive.
items.s: Parks Canada: Travelling the Icefields Parkway

items.q: The Beartooth Highway (US-212) runs from Red Lodge, Montana to which Yellowstone entrance?
items.f: The road is about 68 miles long and was built between 1932 and 1936. It's usually open from Memorial Day weekend to mid-October.
items.s: U.S. Forest Service: Beartooth Highway

items.q: In the 1964 Alaska earthquake, what happened to 20 miles of the Seward Highway?
w: It was buried by a glacier
items.f: The sunken road ended up below the high-water mark of Turnagain Arm.
items.s: Alaska DOT&PF: Seward Highway

items.q: In what year was Glacier's Going-to-the-Sun Road dedicated at Logan Pass?
items.f: The first car crossed the whole road in late 1932, and the dedication ceremony was held on July 15, 1933.
items.s: National Park Service: Going-to-the-Sun Road 75th Anniversary

items.q: Iron Mountain Road is famous for 'pigtail bridges.' What do they do?
items.a: Loop the road a full 360 degrees
items.f: The road has three of these corkscrew bridges, which climb steep slopes in a tight spiral.
items.s: U.S. Forest Service: Black Hills FAQs

items.q: The Blue Ridge Parkway connects which two national parks?
w: Mammoth Cave and Great Smoky Mountains
items.f: The Parkway is 469 miles long. Its mileposts start at 0 near Shenandoah and end at 469 in the Smokies.
items.s: National Park Service: Blue Ridge Parkway Auto Touring

items.q: Which Oregon road, built from 1913 to 1922, is often called America's first scenic highway?
items.f: Sam Hill and Samuel Lancaster built it to show off the Columbia River Gorge's waterfalls and cliffs.
items.s: U.S. Forest Service: Historic Columbia River Highway

items.q: Yosemite's Tioga Road tops out at Tioga Pass at about what elevation?
items.f: It's the highest highway crossing of the Sierra Nevada in California, and snow usually closes it from about November to late May or June.
items.s: National Park Service: Tioga Pass Entrance

items.q: Colorado's 'Million Dollar Highway' (US 550) runs between Ouray and which town?
items.f: It's part of the San Juan Skyway, a loop of about 236 miles that's designated an All-American Road.
items.s: Colorado Department of Transportation: San Juan Skyway

items.q: Alaska's Dalton Highway ends at which oilfield camp near the Arctic Ocean?
items.f: The road runs 414 miles, mostly on gravel, and crosses the Arctic Circle at milepost 115.
items.s: Bureau of Land Management: Dalton Highway

items.q: Yellowstone's Grand Loop Road is shaped like what?
items.f: The Grand Loop is 142 miles long, with a 70-mile upper loop and a 96-mile lower loop.
items.s: National Park Service: Yellowstone & Grand Teton Map

items.q: What kind of traffic is NOT allowed on the Blue Ridge Parkway?
items.f: The speed limit is 45 mph unless posted otherwise. There are no gas stations on the Parkway itself.
items.s: National Park Service: Getting Around the Blue Ridge Parkway

items.q: The Corn Palace, decorated with murals made from corn, is in which town?
items.f: The murals change every year, unless drought or a poor harvest gets in the way.
items.s: Corn Palace (City of Mitchell)

items.q: The Hāna Highway leads to the Kīpahulu District of which national park?
items.f: Kīpahulu is 12 miles past the town of Hāna, and there's no gas in the park, so fill up in Pāʻia.
items.s: National Park Service: Kīpahulu District

items.q: The Dalton Highway crosses the Brooks Range and the Continental Divide at which pass?
items.f: North of the pass, rivers flow to the Arctic Ocean. To the south, they flow toward the Pacific and the Bering Sea.
items.s: Bureau of Land Management: Atigun Pass

items.q: Route 66 celebrates which birthday in 2026?
items.f: The Mother Road got its number in 1926, so its centennial falls in the same year as America's 250th birthday.
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Corridor Preservation Program

items.q: The Seward Highway runs from Anchorage along which inlet famous for beluga whales?
items.f: The highway is an All-American Road, the top designation for a U.S. scenic byway.
items.s: Alaska DOT&PF: Seward Highway

items.q: Which state has the most drivable miles of Route 66?
items.f: About 400 miles of the Mother Road cross Oklahoma, from Quapaw to Texola.
items.s: Oklahoma Department of Transportation

items.q: The Cabot Trail, a famous coastal loop, is in which Canadian province?
items.f: The loop is nearly 300 km around northern Cape Breton Island, and about a third of it runs through Cape Breton Highlands National Park.
items.s: Parks Canada: Cape Breton Highlands Directions

items.q: Road Trip Locals' Grand Trifecta itinerary suggests flying into which city?
items.f: From Bozeman it's about 5 hours to Grand Teton, and about 6.5 hours from Yellowstone to Glacier.
items.s: Road Trip Locals: The Grand Trifecta

items.q: Which road is the highest paved road in North America?
items.f: The road climbs to about 14,130 feet. The mountain was called Mount Evans until 2023.
items.s: Colorado Department of Transportation

items.q: The Great River Road follows which river through 10 states?
items.f: The byway runs from northern Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: America's Byways

items.q: Which bridge carries US 93 over the Colorado River next to Hoover Dam?
items.f: The bridge opened in 2010 and stands nearly 900 feet above the river.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: Public Roads

items.q: Who planned South Dakota's Needles Highway, walking and riding horseback over the route himself?
items.f: The highway was finished in 1922 and squeezes through the narrow Needles Eye Tunnel.
items.s: South Dakota Game, Fish & Parks: Custer State Park Scenic Drives

items.q: 'America the Beautiful' was inspired by the view from which mountain?
items.f: Katharine Lee Bates rode a wagon to the summit in 1893 and wrote the first draft back at her hotel.
items.s: National Park Service: Places of Katharine Lee Bates

items.q: Which highway, announced in 1913, ran from Times Square in New York to Lincoln Park in San Francisco?
items.f: The first route was 3,389 miles long, and less than half of it was improved road.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: The Lincoln Highway

items.q: New Hampshire's Kancamagus Highway (Route 112) runs between Lincoln and which town?
items.f: The highway runs through the White Mountain National Forest, with campgrounds and historic sites along the way.
items.s: U.S. Forest Service: Russell-Colbath Historic Site

items.q: In 1919, a young Dwight Eisenhower joined the Army's first cross-country motor convoy on which road?
items.f: The convoy drove from Washington, DC, to San Francisco. Later, Eisenhower said the trip shaped his support for better highways.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: The Lincoln Highway

items.q: In what year was Route 66 decommissioned as a federal highway?
items.f: Five different Interstates replaced it.
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Overview

items.q: Burma-Shave's famous rhyming roadside signs advertised what?
items.f: The signs ran from 1926 to 1963. At their peak, there were 7,000 sets in 45 states.
items.s: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

items.q: Road Trip Locals' 'Grand Slam' road trip loops through which mountains?
items.f: The 10-day loop starts and ends in Calgary, with stops in Banff, Lake Louise, the Icefields Parkway and Jasper.
items.s: Road Trip Locals: The Grand Slam

items.q: Since 2023, how do you get to Moraine Lake near Lake Louise?
items.a: By shuttle, transit or tour, not your own car
items.f: Parks Canada closed the road to personal vehicles because of congestion and safety concerns. Book shuttles ahead.
items.s: Parks Canada: Visiting Lake Louise and Moraine Lake

items.q: Which highway did Life magazine call 'The Loneliest Road in America' in 1986?
items.f: Nevada embraced the name and created a 'survival guide' that travelers can get stamped along the route.
items.s: Travel Nevada (State of Nevada)

items.q: What was the last section of the Blue Ridge Parkway to be finished?
items.f: The viaduct wraps around Grandfather Mountain in North Carolina. It was built from the top down so no construction road had to be cut into the mountainside.
items.s: National Park Service: History of the Linn Cove Viaduct

items.q: The Florida Keys' Seven Mile Bridge carries which highway?
items.f: Mile Marker 0 in Key West marks the southern end of US 1, which starts in Fort Kent, Maine.
items.s: Federal Highway Administration: U.S. 1, Fort Kent to Key West

items.q: Who called Route 66 'The Mother Road'?
items.f: The nickname comes from his 1939 novel 'The Grapes of Wrath.'
items.s: National Park Service: Route 66 Overview

items.q: Who made the first cross-country trip by car, in 1903?
items.f: Jackson and mechanic Sewall Crocker drove from California to New York in 63 days. Their bulldog, Bud, wore goggles, which the Smithsonian now keeps.
items.s: Smithsonian: America on the Move

items.q: In what year was Big Sur's famous Bixby Creek Bridge built?
items.f: Its 330-foot main span is the largest concrete arch span in California.
items.s: Caltrans: Concrete Arch Bridges of California

items.q: Construction of the Icefields Parkway started in 1931 as what kind of project?
items.f: Canada hired 600 unemployed men, who built the road mostly by hand with horses. Each work crew was allowed only one tractor.
items.s: Parks Canada: A Brief History of the Icefields Parkway

items.q: Why are the drivers of Glacier's historic red buses called 'jammers'?
items.a: For the sound of jamming gears on steep grades
w: They pack in as many riders as possible
items.f: The red buses have carried visitors over Going-to-the-Sun Road since the 1930s.
items.s: National Park Service: Glacier Former Artists-in-Residence

items.q: Which South Dakota road's one-lane tunnels frame views of Mount Rushmore?
items.f: The road's north entrance starts inside the Mount Rushmore National Memorial boundary.
items.s: National Park Service: Iron Mountain Road
